Draft/BIP32 sentence: “With a discrete log, a depth-3 key gives the account's private key and every key below it, and stops there; it reaches neither rule A nor rule B.” Classification: **verified by independent BIP32 reasoning**. Given the depth-3 xpub `(K,c)` at `m/44'/429'/account'`, a discrete log yields the account private scalar `k`. Hardened child derivation is computable from a parent private key: `IL = HMAC-SHA512(c_parent, 0x00‖ser(k_parent)‖be32(i+2^31))`, child `k_i = IL + k_parent mod n`; recursion reaches all descendants under that account, hardened or not. It stops upward/sideways: recovering the `m/44'/429'` parent private key, other account siblings, the master, or `m/8391'/…` would require reversing the hardened HMAC step or knowing the master/parent secret. Rule B is separate because post 1 roots it in `HMAC-SHA512(\"ergo-pq/v1\", bip39Seed)` at [5385-post1-opening.md:31-38](/tmp/claude-1000/-home-scott-bin-ergo-logic/c6b06f96-0ee1-46cc-af7e-1d423aa0f65c/scratchpad/slice-5385r2/thread/5385-post1-opening.md:31), not in any BIP32 node. One wording caveat: “a depth-3 key” should be read as the xpub; public key alone without chain code would not derive non-hardened children, though the discrete-log private key still enables hardened derivation only if the relevant chain code is known.\n\n13.
